quote: In the Bowden trial, which patient populations were identified as responding particularly well to divalproex compared to lithium?
problem: Bowden 1994 could not compare divalproex with lithium in rapid cycling: all eight patients with four or more manic episodes in the prior year were randomized to divalproex. The trial reported only that divalproex was as effective in rapid-cycling patients as in other patients. The mixed-state advantage over lithium comes from a later secondary analysis (Swann 1997).
whyItMatters: Learners and residents would cite a head-to-head subgroup superiority over lithium that the landmark trial never showed. That is a mis-summarised landmark result, taught as an answer key.
evidence: Bowden CL et al., JAMA 1994;271:918-24 (PMID 8120960), abstract: 'all eight patients with four or more manic episodes in the previous year were in the divalproex group ... Divalproex was as effective in rapid-cycling manic patients as in other patients.' Mixed or depressive mania: Swann AC et al., Arch Gen Psychiatry 1997 (secondary analysis).
correction: In the Bowden trial and its secondary analyses, divalproex was effective in which patient subgroups, in whom lithium has historically performed less well?

quote: These two agents were specifically highlighted for providing the best overall balance between therapeutic effect and patient acceptability.
problem: The 2018 Cipriani network meta-analysis did not single out escitalopram and sertraline. Escitalopram, agomelatine and vortioxetine appeared in both its 'more effective' and 'more tolerable' head-to-head lists. Sertraline appeared only in the tolerability list. The escitalopram–sertraline 'best balance' comes from the 2009 Cipriani MANGA analysis (12 drugs).
whyItMatters: Learners would attribute a 2009 finding to the 2018 paper and present it on rounds as the 2018 result. The distractor 'paroxetine and agomelatine' is also half-supported by the 2018 data, which leaves the item ambiguous.
evidence: Cipriani A et al., Lancet 2018;391:1357-66 (PMID 29477251), abstract: head-to-head, more effective were agomelatine, amitriptyline, escitalopram, mirtazapine, paroxetine, venlafaxine and vortioxetine; more tolerable were agomelatine, citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, sertraline and vortioxetine. Cipriani A et al., Lancet 2009;373:746-58 (MANGA) identified sertraline and escitalopram as the best balance.
correction: Escitalopram ranked well on both efficacy and acceptability in the 2018 analysis (as did agomelatine and vortioxetine), and sertraline ranked among the most tolerable; the escitalopram–sertraline 'best balance' pairing itself comes from Cipriani's earlier 2009 analysis of 12 antidepressants.

quote: Based on the study results, which drug demonstrates the highest efficacy but is limited by the worst side-effect profile (lowest acceptability)?
problem: The stem still says amitriptyline had the lowest acceptability, and the keyed feedback now contradicts it: clomipramine was the only agent worse than placebo for dropouts. In head-to-head trials amitriptyline was one of seven agents with the highest dropout rates, not the worst. The earlier fix (A3C1-F001) corrected only the feedback.
whyItMatters: The item contradicts itself, and a learner memorising the stem learns a false ranking.
evidence: Cipriani 2018 (PMID 29477251): clomipramine worse than placebo for acceptability (OR 1.30); amitriptyline, clomipramine, duloxetine, fluvoxamine, reboxetine, trazodone and venlafaxine had the highest dropout rates head-to-head.
correction: Based on the study results, which drug had the highest efficacy odds ratio but was among the agents with the highest dropout rates (poor acceptability)?

quote: The trial demonstrated efficacy and safety in office-based settings, which was foundational for the passage of DATA 2000 and the shift away from exclusive methadone clinic models.
problem: The chronology is reversed. DATA 2000 was enacted in October 2000, before Fudala's results were published (NEJM, September 2003). The trial's data supported FDA approval of Subutex/Suboxone in October 2002, which made office-based prescribing under DATA 2000 possible in practice.
whyItMatters: Learners would misstate the regulatory history of office-based buprenorphine, a common teaching and exam topic.
evidence: Drug Addiction Treatment Act of 2000, Pub. L. 106-310 (enacted Oct 17, 2000); Fudala PJ et al., NEJM 2003;349:949-58; FDA approval of Subutex/Suboxone Oct 8, 2002.
correction: The trial demonstrated efficacy and safety in office-based settings, supporting the 2002 FDA approval of buprenorphine and buprenorphine/naloxone that put DATA 2000's office-based model into practice and moved treatment beyond exclusive methadone clinics.

quote: This is a correct interpretation of the study's impact on the passage of DATA 2000 and the shift to office-based care.
problem: The same reversed chronology as Q1: DATA 2000 (2000) predates the Fudala publication (2003).
whyItMatters: It reinforces a false historical claim.
evidence: DATA 2000 enacted Oct 2000; Fudala NEJM 2003; FDA approval Oct 2002.
correction: This is a correct interpretation of the study's role in the 2002 FDA approval that put DATA 2000's office-based model into practice.

quote: Administering buprenorphine, a partial agonist with high affinity, to a patient not in withdrawal can displace full agonists and precipitate acute withdrawal.
problem: The item keys objective withdrawal (COWS ≥8–12) as a 'critical requirement' for any safe induction and attributes it to Fudala 2003, which did not use COWS. Current guidance also accepts low-dose ('micro') initiation that needs no withdrawal. With fentanyl, precipitated withdrawal can occur even at these COWS thresholds.
whyItMatters: Residents in the fentanyl era would treat standard withdrawal-based induction as the only safe option. They could either precipitate withdrawal with it or leave patients untreated when low-dose initiation fits better.
evidence: ASAM National Practice Guideline for the Treatment of OUD, 2020 Focused Update (low-dose initiation; timing of induction); SAMHSA TIP 63 (2021 update). COWS: Wesson & Ling, J Psychoactive Drugs 2003, not used in Fudala 2003.
correction: Administering buprenorphine, a partial agonist with high affinity, to a patient not in withdrawal can displace full agonists and precipitate acute withdrawal; this applies to standard induction — low-dose ('micro') initiation without withdrawal is an accepted alternative, and after fentanyl use precipitated withdrawal can occur even at these COWS scores.

quote: If the urine is completely negative, the patient might not be in enough withdrawal, potentially leading to precipitated withdrawal if opioids are still on the receptors.
problem: The rationale is internally incoherent. A negative opioid screen implies no recent opioid exposure, so it cannot explain precipitated withdrawal. The real point is that a negative urine is not required, and a positive screen is expected in active OUD.
whyItMatters: It teaches confused reasoning about how induction is timed and what a urine drug screen shows.
evidence: SAMHSA TIP 63: induction is timed to objective withdrawal, not to a negative toxicology screen; a UDS positive for opioids is expected.
correction: A negative urine toxicology is not required; induction is timed to objective withdrawal signs, and a screen positive for opioids is expected in a patient with active OUD.

quote: This structured intervention provides patients with coping strategies and has shown a dramatic 50% reduction in subsequent suicidal acts.
problem: The rationale leaves out two facts. The effect came from the Safety Planning Intervention plus at least two structured follow-up phone calls, not the plan alone. The design was a non-randomized cohort comparison in VA EDs. The result was 3.0% vs 5.3% suicidal behavior over 6 months (OR 0.56), reported as 45% fewer suicidal behaviors.
whyItMatters: Learners would believe that handing over a safety plan alone halves suicidal behavior and could skip the follow-up contact that was part of the tested intervention.
evidence: Stanley B et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2018;75:894-900 (PMID 29998307): SPI+ (SPI plus telephone follow-up), cohort comparison at 9 VA EDs, 3.03% vs 5.29%, OR 0.56 (0.33–0.95).
correction: Paired with structured follow-up phone calls, the intervention was associated with about 45% fewer suicidal behaviors over 6 months (3.0% vs 5.3%; OR 0.56) in a large non-randomized VA emergency-department cohort comparison (Stanley et al., 2018).

quote: DBT remains the most evidence-based treatment, confirmed by multiple meta-analyses including a 2017 JAMA Psychiatry study.
problem: The 2017 JAMA Psychiatry meta-analysis (Cristea et al.) did not rank DBT above other therapies. It found DBT and psychodynamic approaches were the only types more effective than control, with small effects inflated by risk of bias and publication bias. The same deck's Q6 feedback says so correctly, so the two rationales contradict each other.
whyItMatters: The item misattributes a conclusion to a named paper and overstates the certainty of the evidence for DBT versus psychodynamic therapies.
evidence: Cristea IA et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2017;74:319-328 (PMID 28249086): DBT g=0.34, psychodynamic g=0.41, 'effects are small, inflated by risk of bias and publication bias'.
correction: DBT remains one of the best-studied treatments for BPD; a 2017 JAMA Psychiatry meta-analysis found DBT and psychodynamic approaches both more effective than control conditions, though with small effects.

quote: The combination therapy yielded a 60% response rate, which was a modest but notable increase over either monotherapy alone.
problem: In Barlow 2000 the acute combined response (60.3% on the PDSS) was not significantly different from the other groups. Combination therapy's advantage appeared only by the end of maintenance, and after discontinuation the CBT+imipramine arm lost durability (26.3% vs 41.0% for CBT+placebo).
whyItMatters: Learners would believe combination therapy is acutely superior, which the trial did not show, and would miss that adding imipramine undermined CBT's durability.
evidence: Barlow DH et al., JAMA 2000;283:2529-36 (PMID 10815116): 'acute response rate for the combined treatment was 60.3% ... neither was significantly different from the other groups'; 6 months post-discontinuation CGI response 41.0% CBT+placebo vs 26.3% CBT+imipramine.
correction: The combination therapy yielded a numerically higher 60% response rate, but this was not statistically different from the other groups acutely; its advantage emerged during maintenance and was not durable after imipramine was stopped.

quote: The trial was pivotal because it proved that divalproex was not inferior to lithium for acute stabilization.
problem: Bowden 1994 was a placebo-controlled superiority trial with a small lithium arm (n=35 in the ITT analysis, 2:1:2 allocation). It was not designed or powered to establish non-inferiority to lithium.
whyItMatters: It teaches a formal statistical claim (non-inferiority) that the trial did not test.
evidence: Bowden 1994 (PMID 8120960): 2:1:2 randomization; ITT n=68/35/73; both drugs superior to placebo.
correction: The trial was pivotal because both divalproex and lithium outperformed placebo with similar response rates, although it was not designed to formally test non-inferiority.

quote: Which of the following is considered a major absolute contraindication to the use of divalproex mentioned in the trial's clinical pearls?
problem: Under the US label, pregnancy is an absolute contraindication to valproate only for migraine prophylaxis. For bipolar disorder it carries a boxed warning: avoid unless other treatments have failed or are unacceptable. The label's absolute contraindications are hepatic disease, POLG mitochondrial disorders, urea cycle disorders and hypersensitivity.
whyItMatters: On an exam, learners would misidentify the label's absolute contraindications. The practical advice (avoid in pregnancy) is still sound.
evidence: Depakote (divalproex) US prescribing information: Contraindications (hepatic disease, POLG, urea cycle disorders, hypersensitivity, migraine prophylaxis in pregnancy); Boxed Warning (fetal risk).
correction: Which of the following is the most important reason to avoid divalproex, carried as a boxed warning and highlighted in the trial's clinical pearls?

quote: The study confirmed that clozapine remains the most effective agent, standing alone in its superior efficacy compared to all other studied antipsychotics.
problem: Huhn 2019 ranked clozapine highest (SMD −0.89 vs placebo) but concluded that efficacy differences are 'gradual rather than discrete' with low or very low confidence. It excluded treatment-resistant patients, so it does not show clozapine significantly superior to every other agent.
whyItMatters: It overstates the paper and conflates acute multi-episode data with clozapine's established role in treatment resistance.
evidence: Huhn M et al., Lancet 2019;394:939-51 (PMID 31303314): TRS excluded; 'efficacy differences ... gradual rather than discrete'; confidence often low or very low.
correction: Clozapine had the largest effect size versus placebo (SMD −0.89), although the authors judged efficacy differences between drugs to be gradual rather than discrete, and treatment-resistant patients were excluded.
